extracted.intended_audience: members of the Royal Society / natural philosophers and experimentalists (17th-century scientists)
extracted.subtask_description: Reporting experimental and observational accounts in natural philosophy, including methods, observations, and practical recommendations (e.g., mining safety, microscopic anatomy, instrument descriptions). Emphasizes empirical procedure, controls, material details, and observable signs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Mine ventilation as primary cause and control of fire-damp
rubrics_metrics.description: The want of air perpendicularly from the day was the great cause and encourager of this damp; the air that followed down into this pit came down ... after it had been dispersed over all the old hollows and deads of the former work, that were filled up with noisome vapors, thick smothering fogs, and in some places with the smothering damp itself.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess ventilation paths and avoid sinking pits that draw stale air from old hollows/deads; ensure fresh air from surface to prevent accumulation of fire-damp. Note that interruptions of work (e.g., 48 hours) allowed damp to gain strength.

rubrics_metrics.name: Warning signs and indicators of fire-damp
rubrics_metrics.description: Small blueish flame continually moving in crevices; appearances of fire-damp in watery crevices, flashing and darting from side to side, showing rainbow-like colours on the surface of the water; water 'blood-warm' and crevices 'firered'.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Report and monitor visual and olfactory signs (blueish flames, flashes, coloured films on water, foul smoke, noisome smell, rise in water temperature, roaring noises). Use these signs to evaluate pit safety and decide on suspension of work.

rubrics_metrics.name: Practical methods to test and clear fire-damp (historical practices)
rubrics_metrics.description: Employ a man to go down before others, wearing worst rags wet with water, crawling on his belly, carrying a long wand or pole with burning candles to drive and weaken the damp; binding candles to a hook at the rope's end to lower into shaft.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When evaluating recommended procedures, include details of protective measures (wet rags, low posture to avoid gas layer), tools (long pole, candles on hook), and note the risks: candles can be blown out or ignite larger explosions. Document efficacy and incidents (e.g., blasts that scorched men).

rubrics_metrics.name: Emergency response and cessation criteria for dangerous pits
rubrics_metrics.description: When the damp gained great strength and flashed with such force that none durst venture down, the men made no further trial and ceased work; notable violent events included roaring like a bull and throwing men senseless.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include explicit criteria for stopping work: observed violent flashing, extinguishing of test candles with strong flame and foul smoke, roaring noises, physical injuries, or structural displacement (e.g., engine frame moved). Recommend immediate cessation and avoidance of further trial until secure ventilation or other remedies implemented.

rubrics_metrics.name: Microscopic specimen preparation: separation and thin representation
rubrics_metrics.description: I cut asunder with a sharp knife, and using a microscope I severed before my eyes the membrane from it; having taken off these membranes ... I saw very clearly these carneous threads ... When the brain lay spread very thin, cut through with a knife, ... there they appeared like a very clear matter resembling oil.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Report exact specimen preparation: use a sharp knife to separate membranes and represent structures very thinly to reveal internal features. Note how cutting/thin-slicing may produce or reveal matters (e.g., oily appearance) and document whether such appearance is artifact of preparation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Microscopic observation methods and replication across specimens
rubrics_metrics.description: I have used several methods of viewing the particles ... I have divided before my eye ... I have continued my observations for almost a whole month together ... pursuing these observations about the brains of beasts, I was able very plainly to represent to myself the vessels.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Emphasize repeated observations over time, using multiple viewing methods and multiple species (cow, cod-fish, duck, calf, pullet, sheep) to confirm structures. Record methods tried, frequency/duration of observation, and cross-specimen comparisons to strengthen claims.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of comparative specimens to reveal otherwise-invisible structures
rubrics_metrics.description: In the brain of a cod-fish ... I saw those numerous vessels or veins which were very clear, disseminating themselves ... which were 15 or 20 times finer than a single thread of a silkworm.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When one specimen is opaque or unclear, examine alternative species or tissues (e.g., fish brain) whose transparency or structure may reveal fine vessels. Report which taxa yield clearer images and why (e.g., smaller globules, different tissue consistency).

rubrics_metrics.name: Controlled comparison to test medical claims (moxa vs cotton)
rubrics_metrics.description: I have put some of the moxa on fine post-paper, and some cotton likewise, after I had somewhat cut it asunder with scissars, ... The burnings caused on the paper by both were very near alike; and I concluded, that if the burning had any effect in the gout, it proceeded not from any peculiar quality in the moxa, but only from the burning itself.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include controlled experiments to compare claimed therapeutic agents: match sample shape/size, apply to identical mediums, and observe/record effects. Use such controls to separate material-specific effects from effects of the act (e.g., burning) itself.

rubrics_metrics.name: Material selection for dressing wounds: shape and stiffness matter
rubrics_metrics.description: Cotton ... having two flat sides, and consequently every part of it two sharp sides ... cotton being laid upon a wound ... the new matter ... is the more easily cut asunder and dissolved; whereas ... linen rags having roundish parts ... do not so wound the globular parts of the flesh.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluate dressings not only by material but by structure (flat vs roundish fibres), stiffness, and interaction with healing tissue. Prefer softer, rounder-bodied linen rags over cotton for dressing fresh wounds according to these observations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Design and feature criteria for an accurate miniature celestial globe
rubrics_metrics.description: The size of this globe is only of 4 inches diameter. The body is of burnished steel, where all the figures of the constellations are designed in silver-colour, but the stars themselves of all magnitudes are put on in embossed gold. The circles of the longitude of the stars ... are marked by gold-wires; as also the equator, the tropics, and the poplar circles. This globe moves from east to west in 24 hours ... it shows the sun exactly to rise and set as in the great world; also the moon ... shows visibly the first quarter ... her conjunction with the sun ... The meridian serves for a needle, to show the hours ... the 360 degrees of the circle are marked ... the days of the month, where the 365 days are noted. This Globe may generally serve for the whole world, as it can be put to all the elevations of the pole.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When assessing or constructing a model globe, check material and scale, marked astronomical circles (longitude, equator, tropics), representation of star magnitudes, gold/silver detailing, accurate diurnal rotation (24h), demonstrated solar and lunar motions and phases, degree and day scales, and ability to set pole elevation for global applicability. Include a primum mobile winding mechanism with means to accelerate/retard movement.

rubrics_metrics.name: Indicators of diamond deposit quality and characteristics by mine
rubrics_metrics.description: The earth is somewhat yellowish, not unlike the colour of gravel dried; ... diamonds not lying in continued clusters, but frequently so very scattering ... diamonds well shaped, many of them pointed, and of a good lively white water; but it also produces some yellow ones, some brown, and of other colours. ... The mines of Codawillikul ... consist of a reddish earth, inclining to an orange-colour ... They dig about 4 fathoms deep. They afford stones generally of an excellent crystalline water, and crystalline skin ... some of a blue water.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluate deposits by soil colour/texture, depth to reach deposits, presence of smooth pebbles, scatter/distribution (scattered vs clustered), stone shapes (pointed, razor-blade ends), 'water' (clarity) and skin (surface appearance), typical sizes (measured in mangelins), and regional differences. Use these descriptors to appraise likely yield and commercial character of finds.

rubrics_metrics.name: Diamond extraction technique: heating and slaking crusts to reach veins
rubrics_metrics.description: They cut a pit ... before they come to a crust of a mineral stone, ... when they fill the hole with wood, and keep there as hot a fire as they can for 2 or 3 days, till they think it sufficiently heated; then they pour in water till they have quenched it, which also slakes and mollifies both stone and mineral; both being cold, they dig again ... the crust seldom is thicker than 3 or 4 feet, after which they come to a vein of earth ... this they dig all out and search.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Document and evaluate practical mining methods: heat-rock-and-quench technique to slake hard crusts, limited digging depth constrained by water and local engine technology, breaking mineral lumps to find enclosed diamonds, and the creation of local cisterns for washing/processing. Include notes on labour limits and health risks (e.g., bad water causing fevers).
